extra.message: The user-supplied imagelink value from the JSON request body of POST /api/rfivuln (rfi.get('imagelink'), line 15) is passed directly as the URL to requests.get() with no validation, allowlisting, or scheme/host restrictions. This is a Server-Side Request Forgery (Remote File Inclusion) vulnerability: an attacker can make the server fetch internal-only resources (e.g., http://127.0.0.1/ or cloud metadata endpoints such as http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/), and the fetched response body is returned to the attacker.

The user-supplied mathexp value from the JSON request body of POST /api/sstivuln (ssti.get('mathexp'), line 9) is concatenated directly into a Jinja2 Template string that is then rendered (line 12). This enables full Server-Side Template Injection: an attacker can supply template expressions (e.g., {{ 7*7 }} or Python object-traversal payloads) that are evaluated in the server's Python context, leading to remote code execution.

This Host Header Injection allows an attacker to craft requests with a malicious Host header, enabling attacks such as web cache poisoning, password-reset/link manipulation, and cross-site scripting via the injected href attribute.

extra.message: The application is started with app.run(host='0.0.0.0', port=8000, debug=True). Debug mode exposes the interactive Werkzeug debugger console, which permits arbitrary remote code execution once an attacker triggers an exception and obtains or brute-forces the debugger PIN. Binding to all network interfaces makes this remotely exploitable; debug mode must never be enabled on a network-accessible server.

requests.get() is called with verify=False, which disables TLS/SSL certificate verification for the outbound HTTPS request. The server will accept any certificate, including one presented by a man-in-the-middle attacker, allowing interception or tampering with the fetched content.

The user-supplied username from the JSON request body of POST /api/xssreflected (xss.get('username'), line 7) is reflected directly back in the response message via an f-string without any HTML escaping or sanitization. Reflected Cross-Site Scripting results whenever this value is rendered in a browser context, allowing session hijacking and other script-driven attacks.

extra.message: Hardcoded credentials (mike/kaines) are embedded in the application source code and inserted into the USERS database table on startup. Anyone with access to the source code or the database file obtains these credentials, which are also stored in plaintext.

Hardcoded default admin credentials (admin/admin) are embedded in the application source code and inserted into the USERS database table on startup, giving a trivially guessable privileged account. The password is also stored in plaintext rather than hashed.

Raw exception messages from the database execution are returned directly to the client in the response body. These SQL error messages can disclose internal details such as query structure, table names, and column names, providing an attacker with information useful for crafting further injection attacks.
